original_question: A finite group G is called weakly ab-maximal if |H: [H, H]| ⩽ |G: [G, G]| for all H ⩽ G. Do weakly ab-maximal groups have bounded derived length? It is known that weakly ab-maximal groups are direct products of weakly abmaximal p-groups(F. Lisi, L. Sabatini, J. Group Theory, 27(2024), 1203–1217).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.114 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": "A finite group G is called weakly ab-maximal if |H : [H, H]| ⩽ |G : [G, G]| for all H ⩽ G. Do weakly ab-maximal groups have bounded derived length?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the Kourovka Notebook entry essentially verbatim. It has the correct ambient class (finite groups), the exact defining inequality for weakly ab-maximal groups, the correct open question about bounded derived length, and the same nearby contextual remark that weakly ab-maximal groups are direct products of weakly ab-maximal p-groups.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the notation [H,H] and [G,G] should be identified explicitly as the commutator subgroups H' and G'.
The phrase "have bounded derived length" should be unpacked as: there exists an absolute constant d such that every finite weakly ab-maximal group is solvable and has derived length at most d.
The Lisi-Sabatini decomposition into direct products of weakly ab-maximal p-groups is contextual information stated in the notebook entry, but it is not part of the formal problem statement itself.
There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses in this problem.
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute integer d such that every finite group G with |H:[H,H]| ≤ |G:[G,G]| for every subgroup H ≤ G (equivalently, every finite weakly ab-maximal group, where [X,X] denotes the commutator subgroup of X) is solvable of derived length at most d?
justification: arXiv:1401.0300 is the Kourovka Notebook, a collection of open problems, and the draft matches the exact target entry: Problem 21.114. There is no narrower theorem/proposition/conjecture nearby that should replace it. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to make the commutator notation explicit and to interpret "bounded derived length" in the standard uniform sense, namely a bound independent of G. The cited Lisi-Sabatini result is indeed the contextual sentence that appears immediately after the problem, but it remains ancillary to the formal question.
